issues.legal_issue: A transferee pendente lite of property involved in a partition can exercise the transferor’s rights, including seeking an equitable partition.
material_facts: The purchasers acquired interests in fields from parties to the partition proceedings while those proceedings were pending.
The purchasers were in possession of the fields and had acquired title to them.
The transfer of their interests and their claims to the fields were undisputed.
issues.conclusion: The transferees could seek an equitable partition just as their transferors could.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, a transferee pendente lite is bound by the proceedings concerning the transferred interest and is a representative-in-interest of the transferor. A transferee from a party to a partition can exercise the transferor’s rights, including the right to seek an equitable partition. The Court also relied on Rule 10 of Order XXII of the Code of Civil Procedure in recognizing a transferee’s participation rights. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.partition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns partition of property.
predicates.interest_transferred_during_proceeding: A party transferred an interest in the property to another person while the partition proceeding was pending.
predicates.transferor_could_seek_equitable_partitio: The transferor could ask for the property to be divided equitably.

issues.definition: When property is being partitioned, a person who receives an interest from a party during the proceeding may seek the equitable partition that the transferor could seek.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee pendente lite who applies to participate in a pending proceeding must be allowed to be impleaded and heard, and may appeal an order with the appellate court’s leave if not already on the record.
material_facts: The purchasers acquired interests in the property during the pending partition proceedings.
The purchasers sought to have their interests considered, although their names were not included in the decree.
issues.conclusion: A transferee who applies to be impleaded and heard cannot be turned away; an unimpleaded transferee may appeal an order with leave of the appellate court.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 10 of Order XXII of the Code of Civil Procedure recognizes a transferee’s right to apply to be impleaded and heard. A transferee pendente lite is a representative-in-interest of the transferor under section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act. The Court compared the transferee’s position to that of an heir, legatee, or official receiver succeeding to an interest during a proceeding. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.pending_proceeding: A suit or other proceeding is pending.
predicates.interest_transferred_during_proceeding: A party transfers an interest in the subject property to another person while the proceeding is pending.
predicates.transferee_applies_to_join: The transferee applies to be added as a party and to be heard.

issues.definition: If a person acquires an interest during a pending proceeding and applies to participate, that person must be joined and heard.

issues.legal_issue: In a partition referred to a revenue authority, an undisputed transferee pendente lite may seek an equitable allotment, and the authority may consider the transferee’s interest without referring the matter back to the civil court.
material_facts: The partition of land assessed to government revenue was being carried out by a Collector under a civil court decree.
The purchasers had acquired and possessed fields from parties to the partition proceedings during their pendency.
The transfers and the purchasers’ rights were undisputed, but the Collector allotted the purchasers’ fields to another share without considering their request for an equitable allotment.
The other parties did not object to the partition made by the Collector.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers had standing to request an equitable allotment, and the Collector could consider their undisputed interests and make an equitable partition without violating the decree or referring the matter back to the civil court. The existing partition was set aside and the matter remanded for a fresh equitable partition.
issues.legal_principle: Section 54 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires a revenue-assessed estate to be partitioned in accordance with the decree and the law relating to partition or separate possession. The Court held that this permits the Collector, where there is no dispute about a transfer or devolution of interest, to take the affected interests into account and make an equitable allotment. This construction avoids unnecessary referral to the civil court and does not violate the decree or exceed the Collector’s authority. Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act also makes the transferee pendente lite bound by the proceedings while recognizing the transferee as representative-in-interest. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.revenue_authority_partition_proceeding: A civil court decree for partition is being implemented by a revenue authority.
predicates.undisputed_transfer_to_transferee: A party transferred an interest in the property during the proceeding, and the transfer and the transferee’s interest are not disputed.
predicates.transferee_seeks_equitable_allotment: The transferee asks the authority to take the acquired interest into account in dividing the property equitably.

issues.definition: When a revenue authority implements a partition decree and a transferee’s interest is undisputed, the authority may consider that interest in making an equitable allotment requested by the transferee.
